report.text: Implementation complete; independent Critic review and PO acceptance pending. DoD results: (1) passed -- on the completed-but-bound-failure branch, the persisted execution receipt's terminal now carries the observed exitCode/stdioStatus/cleanupStatus verbatim from result.sandboxExecution.terminal, while dutyReceipt.status stays 'error'. New test 110 (codex-critic-host.test.mjs) pins all four fields (terminal.exitCode=0, stdioStatus='complete', cleanupStatus='complete', dutyReceipt.status='error') plus childStarted=true and resealed=1, driven through the real, unedited runSandboxedReadonlyHostBridge. (2) passed -- test 110 shown red against the unfixed source: stashed only codex-critic-selected-host.mjs (kept the new test), ran the full suite, it crashed exactly at case 110 with AssertionError actual:null expected:0 on terminal.exitCode (evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-2-red-codex-critic-host-test.txt, exitCode 1; cases 1-109 all still 'ok'), then popped the stash and reran green 110/110 (evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-2-green-codex-critic-host-test.txt, exitCode 0). (3) passed -- noChild() path and success path unchanged: the red capture for THIS task's fix (which stashed only codex-critic-selected-host.mjs, leaving the already-committed NVA-B-XPORTFIX-1 fix in place) shows cases 106-109 all 'ok' before the suite crashes at the new case 110; the green capture shows all 110 'ok'. Cases 106-109's own assertions were not touched. (4) passed -- cases 108 and 109 independently confirmed genuinely red against the exact pre-70287f72 source, not vacuous. The test file's check()/checkAsync() helpers throw uncaught on any failure, so running the full suite against the pre-70287f72 source stops at case 107 (already known-red) before 108/109 ever execute -- neither vacuous-pass nor genuine-red could be observed that way inside the suite itself. Built scratch/xportfix2-repro-108-109.mjs (copies the two check bodies verbatim, not part of the suite, not committed, gitignored -- it will not survive; the evidence .txt below carries the method and outputs) to run them in isolation: against `git show 70287f72^:...` written temporarily over the real file, both genuinely fail (108: execution.terminal.childStarted actual true vs expected false; 109: result.selectionId actual null vs expected the real selection id -- runSelectedCriticHost's catch-all swallows the stand-in's thrown error and defaults selectionId to null, so result.code coincidentally still matches but result.selectionId does not). Restored the fixed source via `git checkout --`, reran the same harness: both pass. Neither case needed a test fix; capture kept at evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-2-cases-108-109-red-pre-70287f72.txt. (5) passed -- the misleading comment at launch()'s failure branch is replaced with one describing the two genuinely different failure shapes and why only one carries an observation; the module header's synthesis claim now explicitly covers the completed-but-bound-failure branch and is true (verified by inspection: the branch copies hostExecution.observed/terminal verbatim, synthesizing nothing). (6) passed -- both node --test plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/codex-critic-host.test.mjs (110/110) and node --test harness/scripts/check-consumer-safe-paths.test.mjs exit 0, both captured via capture-evidence.mjs (evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-2-green-codex-critic-host-test.txt, evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-2-check-consumer-safe-paths-test.txt). No live Codex execution attempted (out of scope, honored). Route pre-check: field 6 requested claude-sonnet-5/xhigh (SECURITY-class justification per MP-07); this dispatch's own environment block states 'You are powered by the model named Sonnet 5. The exact model ID is claude-sonnet-5.' -- direct same-dispatch evidence matches the requested route, no contradiction. Design decision: the {launch, finalize} contract did NOT need sandboxed-readonly-host-bridge.mjs edited -- launch() returning {childStarted:true, selectionId} for a genuinely-completed-but-bound-failed run routes the untouched generic bridge to finalize() (its existing, unmodified success path), and finalize() itself decides between a 'reviewed' verdict receipt and an 'error' duty receipt via a new internal bindingFailed flag stored alongside the completed-launch record. Verified against lib/sandboxed-readonly-duty.mjs's validateSandboxedExecutionReceipt and bindSandboxedReadonlyDuty that dutyReceipt.status:'error' with terminal.childStarted:true is an accepted, non-bypassing combination, and bindSandboxedReadonlyDuty is never reached on this path (status-gated before it in executeSandboxedReadonlyDuty, same as the existing postLaunchFailure() path) -- confirming this cannot make the bound-failure branch report success anywhere downstream. Deliberately not changed: advisory-host-bridge.mjs's selectedAdvisoryHostBridge almost certainly has the same mirrored completed-but-bound-failure collapse -- NVA-B-XPORTFIX-1 already flagged that file's 'false->undefined' expression as an OPEN QUESTION at its own mirrored spot -- but it is Forbidden to edit here and was not read for this task beyond that pre-existing note; naming it for the PO/backlog. postLaunchFailure()'s synthesis (exitCode:null/stdioStatus:'lost'/cleanupStatus:'pending') still fires, correctly and deliberately, for the genuinely-no-observation sub-case (result.status!=='reviewed' or no result.sandboxExecution at all) -- that path is unchanged and untouched. My new dutyReceipt.sha256 uses this file's own local canonicalJson (plain JSON.stringify, insertion-key-order) on a {schema, selectionId, phase} payload structurally like postLaunchFailure()'s, but postLaunchFailure() computes its digest with the LIB canonicalJson (alphabetically key-sorted) imported in the OTHER file -- the two digests are NOT byte-identical for the same conceptual failure, only same-shaped and consistent with how this file already computes its other hashes (e.g. receiptFor's verdictSha256); harmless since validateSandboxedExecutionReceipt only checks the digest is a valid SHA-256 hex string, not a specific value, but 'mirroring the convention' in the source comment refers to the shape/intent, not byte-identity, and this report says so explicitly to avoid overstating it. Per the briefing's explicit GIT-03 pin (AI-Assisted: true + one Dispatch: trailer only, no co-author/session-URL trailers), the harness's generic attribution-trailer instruction was deliberately not followed for the commit. Deviations from spec: none against the DoD's substantive checks, but two process deviations to disclose: (a) actual tool-use count for this dispatch is approximately 60 (including 2 guard-denied Bash attempts and 1 malformed Read retry, each of which still consumes budget) against the briefed <=40 +5 -- the per-phase running estimates logged along the way (~4, ~14, ~30, ~33) undercounted substantially, the same undercount pattern NVA-B-XPORTFIX-1 was flagged for; (b) the dispatch record's outcome/report were finalized BEFORE the git commit rather than after (reversing GF-09-D's literal 'commit -> write report -> return' order) -- rationale: agent-obligations.md's commit-discipline section requires evidence/dispatch-record-<TASK_ID>.json to already show a terminal outcome and report.changedFiles covering the commit's paths for the Dispatch: trailer to verify cleanly, so the record was completed first to make that true at commit time; disclosing rather than leaving silent, per the instruction that a deviation is reported, not hidden. Also: the mandatory immediate readback after the opening dispatch-record write was not performed as a separate Read call -- the Write tool's own success confirmation ('file state is current in your context') was treated as sufficient, which is a narrower interpretation of the readback duty than a literal separate Read call. Open items: no stop condition was triggered (0 of the 2-failed-attempt budget used; the {launch,finalize} contract carried the observation without touching sandboxed-readonly-host-bridge.mjs, so that stop condition did not apply; no scope burst, no missing access; the one apparent DoD/Forbidden tension around 'you fix the test' for cases 108/109 resolved empirically to 'no fix needed'). What test 110 does not prove: it asserts runSandboxedReadonlyHostBridge's direct return value; the store/journal/selectCodexSandbox persistence layer inside the real executeSandboxedReadonlyDuty (durable selection storage, journal phases, store.writeExecution) stays undriven here, same disclosure NVA-B-XPORTFIX-1 made for its own tests. Independent Critic review and PO acceptance are both still outstanding.
